key_insight: Compass treats prostate micro-ultrasound as a multi-view video stream, using rotational context plus biopsy-time frames to improve cancer detection beyond single-image analysis.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help clinicians and AI systems better identify prostate cancer on micro-ultrasound by leveraging the same kind of 3D context expert readers use in practice.
method: Models each micro-ultrasound study as a sequence of 2D images
Combines rotational sweep videos with frames captured during biopsy
Uses an angle-conditioned transformer to aggregate evidence and output frame-level and study-level risk scores
evidence_signal: The model was trained and evaluated on a multi-center clinical trial dataset of micro-ultrasound studies and compared against published AI baselines and expert risk scores.
watch_item: Performance may depend on access to consistent multi-view video acquisitions and accurate probe-angle information, which could affect real-world deployment.
paper_title: Compass: Prostate Cancer Detection Needs Multi-View Context
